evals.prompt: We need a data entry app for 200 users accessing standard Dataverse tables. What licensing do we need?
evals.expected_output: Agent evaluates per-user vs per-app licensing for 200 users accessing Dataverse, and considers whether Code Apps are involved (which require Premium).
expectations: Agent identifies that Dataverse access requires Premium licensing (not covered by M365 seeded)
Agent evaluates per-user Premium ($20/user/month) vs per-app ($5/user/app/month) licensing
Agent recommends per-app licensing as more cost-effective for a single app with 200 users ($5 vs $20 per user)
Agent mentions pay-as-you-go ($10/active user/app/month) as an alternative if adoption is uncertain
Agent notes that if the app is a Code App, Premium licensing is required regardless
Agent may mention API request limits (40,000/day for Premium, 6,000/day for per-app pay-as-you-go) as a capacity consideration

evals.prompt: 5 users need an app with custom connectors, AI Builder, and Power Automate flows. What licenses should we get?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends Power Apps Premium per-user for the 5 users, notes AI Builder capacity requirements (Copilot Credits), and addresses Power Automate licensing separately.
expectations: Agent recommends Power Apps Premium (per-user) since custom connectors require Premium
Agent notes that AI Builder consumes AI Builder credits (seeded with Premium until Nov 2026) or Copilot Credits
Agent warns about the Nov 2026 deadline when seeded AI Builder credits are removed
Agent addresses Power Automate licensing separately — flow owner needs Power Automate Premium if flows use premium connectors
Agent considers whether a Copilot Credits add-on or pay-as-you-go is needed for AI Builder usage beyond seeded credits
Agent does NOT recommend per-app licensing as the primary option when custom connectors and AI Builder are involved (per-user is simpler at this scale)
